meeting_window.summary: The meeting focused on setting up and testing multi-channel recording equipment, discussing data storage, transcription methods, and future improvements.
key_points: Successfully conducted initial multi-channel recordings with three participants reading digits.
Identified needs for a equipment cabinet, improved pre-amps for wired headsets, and more disk space for recordings.
Discussed software improvements for data management and audio processing (resampling, compression).
Planned to evaluate internal vs. external transcription services and methods for generating transcriber-friendly audio.
Explored the potential for using multiple microphones for speaker location and noise cancellation, despite external skepticism.
open_questions: What is the optimal bit depth and compression method for audio recordings?
How to efficiently manage and store large volumes of multi-channel audio data?
What is the most effective and cost-efficient method for transcribing multi-channel meeting recordings?
How to recruit more diverse speakers for future recordings?

meeting_window.summary: The meeting established the initial plan for transcribing meeting recordings. The team discussed transcription tools, personnel, data formats, and the specific requirements for the transcripts, such as including speaker labels and stress marking.
key_points: The main topic was establishing a process for transcribing recorded meetings.
Jane (fe008) is confirmed as the lead for transcription efforts.
The team decided to evaluate 'Transcriber', a tool from a French group, as the primary software for this task.
A plan was made to investigate using undergraduate students for transcription to handle the expected volume of work.
It was agreed that the initial transcription would include word-level text, speaker labels, and stress/prominence marking.
The team discussed data formats and decided that detailed time-alignment could be automated later using the close-talk microphone data.
open_questions: Will the 'Transcriber' tool meet the project's needs?
What is the cost and process for hiring student transcribers?
Will the speech recognition accuracy from far-field microphones be sufficient for effective information retrieval?

action_items.title: Set up recording equipment for multi-channel recording
action_items.detail: Continue setting up and refining the multi-channel recording equipment. Currently supports 3 participants, with potential for 8-9 with headset mics. Requires addressing cabinet and pre-amp issues.
action_items.evidence: We're doing this recording so we show we can - we're capable of doing recording (836.538-840.134).

action_items.title: Acquire a cabinet for recording equipment
action_items.detail: Purchase or build a cabinet with doors to house the recording equipment, preventing tampering and improving organization. Estimated cost: $100-$200.
action_items.evidence: We need to do that. It's on a list of things to do. (343.176-349.322).

action_items.title: Address amplification problem for wired headsets
action_items.detail: Resolve the issue of noisy pre-amps for wired headsets. Options include buying commercial pre-amps or improving the existing self-built unit.
action_items.evidence: there's this amplification problem. I built this thing, it's - that's - it's very noisy. (432.827-442.529).

action_items.title: Acquire more disk space for recordings
action_items.detail: Obtain additional disk space (e.g., 40-50 GB) to accommodate large volumes of multi-channel audio recordings (1-2 GB/hour).
action_items.evidence: we definitely need to go buy uh you know forty gig - fifty gig of drive - drive space. (1087.575-1095.212).

action_items.title: Improve software for recording and data management
action_items.detail: Refine software for resampling, transferring data to other machines, organizing storage, and selecting active channels to optimize file size and workflow.
action_items.evidence: I would like to work out some of the software issues a little more completely. (915.636-920.569).

action_items.title: Conduct more 'read numbers' tasks
action_items.detail: Generate and conduct additional 'read numbers' tasks to collect more speech data, especially from a wider range of speakers.
action_items.evidence: I think we should read some more (1443.098-1448.862).

action_items.title: Transcribe recorded meetings
action_items.detail: The project requires word-level transcripts with speaker identification for training and testing speech recognition models. This is the main task for the transcription effort.
action_items.evidence: we need to transcribe these meetings... to do training and test and so on. (540.561-547.470)

action_items.title: Generate single-channel merged audio for transcribers
action_items.detail: Develop a process to create a single, high-quality, merged audio file from multi-channel recordings to simplify transcription for human transcribers.
action_items.evidence: probably getting some kind of single channel merged sum data or something so that you can give a simple sound file of some sort to a transcriber (1903.829-1917.556).

action_items.title: Investigate lossless audio compression (Shorten)
action_items.detail: Explore the use of lossless audio compression tools like 'Shorten' to reduce the file size of recordings, especially for silent sections.
action_items.evidence: we could probably just run Shorten on them or something and it will get a big win. (1246.328-1250.914).

action_items.title: Investigate optimal bit depth for recording
action_items.detail: Analyze whether recording at a higher bit depth (e.g., 24-bit) or using different 16-bit ranges improves audio quality, particularly for microphones with low gain.
action_items.evidence: Maybe we shouldn't've subsampled it down to sixteen bits for our first try. (1292.558-1296.915).

action_items.title: Re-enable sound card for audio output on recording machine
action_items.detail: Re-enable the built-in sound card on the recording machine to allow direct audio playback and monitoring.
action_items.evidence: That - that card - that machine's got sound - They've got a sound blaster built into it. ... I just disabled it (1385.827-1392.882).

action_items.title: Recruit more diverse speakers for recordings
action_items.detail: Actively seek out and encourage participation from a more diverse group of speakers, including women, for future meeting recordings to ensure representative data.
action_items.evidence: he's - he's - he's got at least one woman. ... And we're - we have a little problem of no women (1570.759-1577.130).

action_items.title: Select and set up transcription software
action_items.detail: The team needs to choose a transcription tool. 'Transcriber', a Tcl/Snack-based tool from a French group found via U_Penn/LDC, was identified as the first candidate. Adam will download and evaluate it with Jane. The possibility of using Adam's PC foot pedals was also discussed.
action_items.evidence: I will check it and try to download it And uh see what it looks like. (1771.342-1775.353)

action_items.title: Investigate resources for transcription assistance
action_items.detail: For the long term, the project will need more transcribers. Jane will investigate using undergrads (for credit or pay) and will consult with Susan Ervin-Tripp for recommendations on how to proceed and estimate costs.
action_items.evidence: I can ask Susan Ervin-Tripp what she would recommend on that. (907.495-910.523)

action_items.title: Collect potential user queries for meeting retrieval
action_items.detail: Collect potential queries that users might ask about the meetings. This will help guide the development of the information retrieval component of the Meeting Recorder application.
action_items.evidence: if over the next couple of days you find yourself wondering what we talked about in the meeting, write down the sort of query you'd like to make. (1834.017-1836.280)

method_changes.before: Ad-hoc setup with wires and open equipment.
method_changes.after: Equipment housed in a cabinet with doors, and cables managed under a mat.
method_changes.reason: To prevent tampering, improve aesthetics, and facilitate easier setup for meetings.
method_changes.evidence: The idea is that this gets replaced by a cabinet with doors, so that - so that it's not open to fiddling. (327.720-334.462).

method_changes.before: PDA placed in the middle of the table.
method_changes.after: Consider placing the PDA in front of each speaker to match acoustics, or keep it in the middle for single PDA scenarios.
method_changes.reason: To optimize acoustics for individual PDA use, while acknowledging flexibility for shared PDA use.
method_changes.evidence: one thing we may wanna do is put the fake P_D_A right in front of someone instead of in the middle of the table like we have it now. (723.835-731.306).

method_changes.after: Word-level transcription will also include marking of prominent/stressed words.
method_changes.reason: It is easy for the transcriber (Jane) to do during the first pass and the data could be valuable for improving information retrieval or for prosody research.
method_changes.evidence: it really is just as easy to put the stress in at that point. (2273.141-2275.878)

experiment_todos.description: Test the hypothesis that multiple microphones at close distance are useless for noise cancelling, contrary to a statement made at a DARPA Communicator meeting.
experiment_todos.evidence: multiple microphones at a distance of less than three feet or something like that were totally useless, completely irrelevant. (562.248-572.214).

experiment_todos.description: Investigate speaker location detection using multiple microphones as a potential justification for their use in proposals.
experiment_todos.evidence: Do they believe you can get speaker location out of it? Cuz that's - that's one way we could sneak it in. (693.579-698.609).

next_meeting_focus: Review the evaluation of the 'Transcriber' tool.
Discuss findings on transcription resources and costs.
Continue recording meetings to stabilize the process and gather more data.
